Purpose and exclusions

Send each client only relevant state while preserving gameplay correctness. Begin with generic Actor replication, then measure before choosing Iris or Replication Graph; do not enable both.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Add read-only counters to WBP_Diagnostics for net role, ping, current zone/epoch, relevant actor counts and received revision.
  2. Set owner-only replication on private character projections; inspect remote clients for inventory/currency leaks.
  3. Configure development network emulation using the installed engine network emulation settings/console help; record actual commands and verify whether latency applies per direction.
  4. Run the same route at no impairment, 100ms RTT, 200ms RTT with jitter, and 2% loss; the exact emulation knob syntax is an installed-engine verification task.
  5. Record captures from server plus two geographically separate or separately hosted clients, not only multi-PIE windows in one process.
  6. Do not change Actor tick, update frequency and relevancy all at once; change one controlled variable and compare regression outcomes.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Replication, interest management and measured scale. Rule owner: URPGReplicationPolicy. This asset’s role is Send each client only relevant state while preserving gameplay correctness. Begin with generic Actor replication, then measure before choosing Iris or Replication Graph; do not enable both.

  1. Separate public world facts, owner-only character facts and cosmetic cues before choosing replication settings.
  2. Generic replication sends movement and approved properties/RPCs; client sprite playback resolves compact state instead of replicating every sprite frame.
  3. Resource actors become dormant when stable and explicitly wake on claim/depletion changes; late relevant clients receive the correct state, not only a past multicast event.
  4. Measure actor/channel counts, bytes, RPCs, server tick and client render cost with representative AI/loot/projectiles; control the same scene and population for comparisons.
  5. Profile generic baseline first. Select either Iris or Replication Graph in an isolated branch only when installed support and actual measurements justify migration.
  6. Retest owner privacy, late join, dormancy wake, loss and zone handoff after every optimization. Never hide a valid combat target on the server because a client did not render it.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_LoadTest / distributed clients / latency-jitter-loss profiles. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Resource wakes from dormancy -> all newly relevant clients see depletion and cannot claim a stale generation.
Loss of cosmetic event -> later state converges without repeating rewards.
High latency inventory click -> pending state persists; no optimistic currency authority.
Remote player disappears outside interest radius -> quest/reward credit uses server policy, not visual presence.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
